secrets.name: GOOGLE_ROUTES_API_KEY
secrets.purpose: Lets the Worker compare driving with bus, walking, biking, or scooter routes. The key stays server-side and never appears in a page.
steps: In the LVBT Google Cloud project, enable the Routes API and billing for the project.

Create a server API key named lvwwd.org Routes. Set Application restrictions to None because Cloudflare Worker egress IPs are not fixed and website referrer restrictions do not apply to server calls. Under API restrictions, allow only Routes API. The key stays in a Worker secret; do not put it in site vars or browser code.
In Google Cloud Quotas, set the Routes API Compute Routes daily quota to 1,000 requests. The Worker also caps usage at 1,000 provider requests per day and 30 comparisons per IP per hour.
Paste the key at this command's prompt. After deployment, verify a real comparison on /go/compare.
secrets.patternHint: A Google API key has at least 20 characters and no spaces.

secrets.name: LVBT_BEEHIIV_API_KEY
secrets.purpose: Enrolls people who explicitly choose the LVBT newsletter on Home or My week, with an email confirmation step. Never sent to a browser.
steps: Sign in to the existing LVBT Beehiiv account and open Settings, then Integrations and API keys.
Use an API key with subscription write access to the existing LVBT publication. A maintainer can reuse the authorized LVBT key or create a key for lvwwd.org.
Paste the key at this command's prompt. Never put it in site vars or browser code.
After deployment, subscribe an address you control, confirm the email, and verify that Beehiiv shows it as active.
secrets.patternHint: A Beehiiv API key has at least 20 characters and no spaces.

secrets.name: LVBT_BEEHIIV_PUBLICATION_ID
secrets.purpose: Selects the existing LVBT newsletter publication for explicit subscription requests.
steps: In the existing LVBT Beehiiv publication, open Settings, then Integrations.
Copy the Publication ID shown there; it starts with pub_. Use the existing LVBT publication, not a new campaign newsletter.
Paste that ID at this command's prompt. Preview Workers should use a separate test publication if direct signup is enabled there.
secrets.patternHint: A Beehiiv publication ID starts with pub_ followed by its UUID.

secrets.name: RESEND_API_KEY
secrets.purpose: Sends each participant's "Open my week" link by email from hello@lvwwd.org.
steps: Sign in to Resend at https://resend.com/login. If you have no account, sign up at https://resend.com/signup with your @lasvegasfortransit.org address and ask a maintainer to invite you to the LVBT team.
Open the existing LVBT domain at https://resend.com/domains/c3eed87b-e72c-4235-85fd-af148cbe0121. It uses North Virginia (us-east-1). Check that its current status is Verified before continuing.

If the domain is Pending, check its DNS records in Cloudflare: TXT resend._domainkey has the full p= value shown by Resend; DNS-only CNAME rsend points to rsend.forge.rmta.net; DNS-only CNAME send points to send.forge.rmta.net. TXT _dmarc with v=DMARC1; p=none; is recommended. Then click Verify DNS Records in Resend and wait for Verified. This domain does not use the older SES MX or SPF records.
Open https://resend.com/api-keys and click "Create API Key". Name it lvwwd.org Worker, choose the permission "Sending access", choose the domain lvwwd.org, and click "Add".
Copy the key, which starts with re_ and is shown only once, and paste it at this command's prompt.
secrets.patternHint: A Resend API key starts with re_ and has no spaces.

secrets.name: TURNSTILE_SECRET
secrets.purpose: Lets the Worker ask Turnstile whether a sign-up or a "Get my link" request came from a person.
secrets.neededFor: the bot check on Sign up to win and Get my link
steps: Open Turnstile in the Cloudflare dashboard with the "Las Vegans for Better Transit" account.

Click the widget named LVWWD production signup. If there is none, click "Add widget", type the widget name LVWWD production signup, add the hostname lvwwd.org under "Hostname management", choose the widget mode "Managed", leave pre-clearance off, and click "Create".
Leave the Site Key alone for now: it is public and goes into TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY in apps/deploy/cloudflare.config.ts, which this command shows later.
Copy the Secret Key, which is private and starts with 0x, and paste it at this command's prompt.
secrets.patternHint: A Turnstile secret key starts with 0x.

secrets.name: ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN
secrets.purpose: Names the Cloudflare Access team whose signed sign-in tokens the Worker accepts for the admin views.
secrets.neededFor: the volunteer admin views at lvwwd.org/admin
steps: Open Cloudflare One at https://one.dash.cloudflare.com/ and choose the "Las Vegans for Better Transit" account.

On Overview, find Account details. It shows the Team domain (for LVBT, lvbt.cloudflareaccess.com) and the Team name ("Las Vegans for Better Transit"), which is only a label. This secret needs the domain.
Copy the Team domain, without https://, and paste it at this command's prompt.
secrets.patternHint: A team domain looks like lvbt.cloudflareaccess.com, without https://.

secrets.name: ACCESS_AUD
secrets.purpose: The audience tag of the lvwwd.org volunteer admin application, so the Worker accepts only tokens Access issued for it.
secrets.neededFor: the volunteer admin views at lvwwd.org/admin
steps: First, the Google Group that decides who gets in. At https://admin.google.com, go to Menu → Directory → Groups. If wwd-admin@lasvegasfortransit.org is listed, go on. Otherwise click "Create group": Group name lvwwd.org volunteer admin, Group email wwd-admin (domain lasvegasfortransit.org), Description "Volunteers who can open the lvwwd.org admin pages", Group owner yourself. Click "Next", tick "Security", click "Next", choose "Restricted", set "Who can join the group" to "Only invited users", leave external members off, and click "Create Group". Then "Add members" with each volunteer's @lasvegasfortransit.org address, and your own so you can test the sign-in. Personal Gmail addresses cannot sign in, even in the group.

Open Cloudflare One at https://one.dash.cloudflare.com/ with the "Las Vegans for Better Transit" account and go to Access controls → Applications. If "lvwwd.org volunteer admin" is listed, skip to the last step.

Click "Create new application" at the top right (an account with no applications shows only a list of prerequisites; the button is still there). In the "Add an application" dialog, under "Self-hosted and private", choose the "Public DNS" tab (not "Private destinations"), then "Continue with Self-hosted and private".

Under "Destinations", fill in three public hostname rows ("+ Add public hostname" adds a row), each with Subdomain empty and lvwwd.org chosen in the Domain dropdown, and the paths admin, admin/* and api/admin/*. A path does not cover the paths under it, so all three are needed. If you see a "Private IPs" row instead, click "+ Add public hostname" and remove the empty private row. Leave "Allow access through browser-based RDP, SSH, or VNC sessions" off.

Under "Access policies", pick lvwwd.org volunteer admin allow in "Add current policies" if it exists; otherwise click "Create new policy", name it exactly lvwwd.org volunteer admin allow, set the action to "Allow", and add the Include rule "Google Workspace groups" = wwd-admin@lasvegasfortransit.org. If "Google Workspace groups" is not offered, Google Workspace sign-in is not connected yet; use an "Emails" rule with the volunteers' addresses for now.

Under "Authentication" (Identity tab), turn off "Accept all available identity providers", choose only "Google Workspace" in "Choose available identity providers", and turn on "Apply instant authentication". Leave "Authenticate with Cloudflare One Client" off.
Under "Details", set Name to exactly lvwwd.org volunteer admin and keep Session Duration at "24 hours". Click "Create".
Open the application's "Configure" page, then the "Additional settings" tab. Copy "Application Audience (AUD) Tag", 64 lowercase letters and digits, and paste it at this command's prompt.
secrets.patternHint: An AUD tag is 64 lowercase letters and digits.

secrets.name: VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY
secrets.purpose: Signs every saved-plan reminder notification, so push services deliver it as coming from lvwwd.org. The Worker works out the public key from it, and a new key would stop every browser's reminders, so setup generates it only when it is missing.
secrets.patternHint: A VAPID private key is 32 bytes in base64url: 43 letters, digits, - and _.

secrets.name: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN
secrets.purpose: Lets the Deploy workflow publish the Worker on every merge to main.
steps: Make it an account API token, which belongs to the LVBT account rather than to you, so deploys keep working after you leave. Creating one needs the Super Administrator role or the API Token Provisioning capability on the account.
In the Cloudflare dashboard, choose the "Las Vegans for Better Transit" account and go to Manage Account → "Account API Tokens". Click "Create Token", then "Create Custom Token".
Name it lvwwd.org deploy (GitHub Actions).

Under "Permissions", add three rows: "Account", "Workers Scripts", "Edit"; "Account", "Account Settings", "Read"; and "Zone", "Workers Routes", "Edit". The deploy applies no migrations, so it needs no D1 permission.
Under "Zone Resources", choose "Include", then "Specific zone", then lvwwd.org.

Leave the expiration empty, so deploys keep working. Click "Continue to summary", then "Create Token". Copy the token, which Cloudflare shows only once, and paste it at this command's prompt; it is stored as the production environment secret CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN in GitHub. The Deploy workflow also sets CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, which cf uses to select the LVBT account.
secrets.patternHint: A Cloudflare API token is at least 40 characters with no spaces.

secrets.name: CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID
secrets.purpose: Tells the Deploy workflow which Cloudflare account owns the Worker.

secrets.name: TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID
secrets.purpose: Identifies the LVBT Twilio account for phone confirmation and morning texts.
steps: Open https://console.twilio.com in the LVBT account. Copy the Account SID from Account Info. Use an LVBT-owned account, not a personal account.
secrets.patternHint: An account SID starts with AC and has 32 hexadecimal characters.

secrets.name: TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN
secrets.purpose: Authenticates Twilio requests and verifies signed STOP and delivery callbacks.
steps: In the LVBT Twilio console, open Account Info and reveal the Auth Token. Paste it only at this setup prompt.
secrets.patternHint: Use the Auth Token from the same LVBT Twilio account.

secrets.name: TWILIO_MESSAGING_SERVICE_SID
secrets.purpose: Uses the registered LVBT sender and Advanced Opt-Out for daily reminders.
steps: In Twilio Messaging → Services, select or create the Week Without Driving service. Add an LVBT-owned SMS sender and complete its required US sender registration before enabling reminders.

Enable Advanced Opt-Out with STOP, START and HELP responses. The HELP response should name LVBT and wwd@lasvegasfortransit.org. Set incoming messages to POST https://lvwwd.org/api/sms/webhook. The Worker also sets this URL as each message status callback.
Copy the Messaging Service SID. Keep SMS_REMINDERS_ENABLED=false until the real-phone checks in docs/operations/how-to/set-up-production.md pass.
secrets.patternHint: A messaging service SID starts with MG and has 32 hexadecimal characters.

secrets.name: TWILIO_VERIFY_SERVICE_SID
secrets.purpose: Confirms ownership of a mobile number before storing a text reminder subscription.
steps: In Twilio Verify → Services, select or create the LVBT Week Without Driving service. Set the friendly name to LVBT Week Without Driving, use six-digit SMS codes, enable Fraud Guard, and restrict SMS verification geography to the United States.
Copy the Verify Service SID. The Verify service and Messaging service must belong to the Account SID configured above.
secrets.patternHint: A Verify service SID starts with VA and has 32 hexadecimal characters.

vars.name: TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY
vars.purpose: The public Turnstile site key the Worker writes into the Sign up and Get my link pages. Set it in apps/deploy/cloudflare.config.ts and its Wrangler fallback mirror.
vars.neededFor: the bot check on Sign up to win and Get my link

vars.name: VAPID_SUBJECT
vars.purpose: The contact push services use to reach LVBT about its reminder notifications: mailto:wwd@lasvegasfortransit.org.

vars.name: EVENT_REMINDERS_ENABLED
vars.purpose: Keeps saved-plan browser reminders off until a real production phone has received and opened a test notification.
vars.neededFor: preventing event-specific notifications before their delivery test passes

vars.name: SMS_REMINDERS_ENABLED
vars.purpose: Keeps phone enrollment and daily texts disabled until a registered Twilio sender and real-phone acceptance checks are complete.
vars.neededFor: releasing optional morning texts after provider acceptance

vars.name: SMS_ORIGIN
vars.purpose: Canonical origin for private My week SMS links and signed Twilio callbacks. Production uses https://lvwwd.org; an isolated SMS preview must use its own HTTPS origin.
vars.neededFor: opening the same database-backed My week session that sent a text

forbidden.name: PREVIEW_ADMIN_KEY
forbidden.reason: This retired preview credential must not be deployed. All admin views require Cloudflare Access.

forbidden.name: PREVIEW_DRAW_ANYTIME
forbidden.reason: It lets the prize draw run before October 14, so it belongs only on the workers.dev preview.

forbidden.name: PREVIEW_SHOW_LINKS
forbidden.reason: It puts each participant's private "Open my week" link into API responses, so it belongs only on the workers.dev preview.

forbidden.name: CHECKIN_PREVIEW_DAY
forbidden.reason: It makes the Worker treat another day as today for check-ins, so it belongs only on the workers.dev preview.

forbidden.name: BOT_CHECK
forbidden.reason: BOT_CHECK=off disables the Turnstile check on public sign-up and link requests and must never be deployed to production.
